note: No dubIS audio section. Bucket = speakers, buzzers, microphones, vibration motors (LCSC's analogous 'Audio Products / Vibration Motors' is scored {Other}) PLUS audio amplifier modules and headphone/audio jacks, where dubIS's own description rules do better than a blanket Other. No single parent; abstain beats pinning the whole bucket to Other.

Industrial grab-bag: motor drives, contactors, PLC I/O modules, actuators, solenoids, remote-control transmitters/receivers, signal towers. None of the 21 sections covers this family and the contents scatter across several (a signal tower is arguably LEDs, a drive board arguably Development Boards). LCSC's comparable 'Industrial Control Electrical' is scored {Other} only because that bucket is much narrower.

Batteries, packs, holders, chargers, AC/DC desktop and enclosed supplies, DC/DC converters. 'ICs - Power / Voltage Regulators' is an IC section (LDOs, switchers, load switches) - a coin cell or a 240W desktop PSU filed there is a misfile, not a coarse answer. LCSC's comparable 'Battery Products' is scored {Mechanical & Hardware, Connectors, Other}, i.e. three parents, which is the table saying it has no single answer.

Fuses, fuse holders, circuit breakers, MOVs, GDTs, PTC resettable fuses and TVS diodes. Only the TVS/ESD leaves have a dubIS home (ICs - ESD Protection / Diodes); fuses and breakers have none. The DIGIKEY_PATH table deliberately labels each Circuit Protection path separately (ICL, Surge Suppression ICs, Thermal Cutoffs, TVS/Thyristors) and never the umbrella - same judgement here. Needs subcategory rows, not a parent row.

1:1 with dubIS's Connectors, and CATEGORY_RULES already key on connector vocabulary (connector/header/receptacle/terminal block/IC socket), so the two agree. Residual tail (cable assemblies, board spacers) is small relative to the bucket; LCSC scores cables {Other, Connectors, Mechanical & Hardware} but the umbrella itself is unambiguously connectors.

dubIS's section is the same family (boards, kits, programmers) and its rules already fire on eval board / dev kit / starter kit / ST-Link / J-Link. Not verified because Mouser's bucket also carries hand tools, test equipment, breadboards/perfboard and enclosures, which dubIS's rules leave in Other - a reviewer may want those split out by subcategory.

Same name, same domain: MOSFETs, IGBTs, thyristors/SCR/TRIAC, SiC/GaN devices, discrete modules. Not verified because Mouser's umbrella also contains Diodes, which dubIS keeps in its own section - a 'Discrete Semiconductors > Diodes' subcategory row should exist before this parent row is trusted for diodes.

Relays, solenoids, motors/actuators, encoders, lamps and signalling devices. dubIS has no electromechanical section (LCSC scores 'Relays' {Other}), but the bucket also holds encoders (Switches/Sensors in the LCSC table) and LED lamps (LEDs) where the description rules do better than a blanket Other. Cannot place the umbrella from its words alone.

MCUs/SoCs, system-on-module and wireless/IoT modules, single-board computers, FPGA/CPLD kits. The existing tables split exactly this three ways: 'Embedded Processors & Controllers' and 'System On Chip (SoC)' -> ICs - Microcontrollers, 'IoT/Communication Modules' / 'Functional Modules' -> {Other, Development Boards, ICs - Interface}. Any single parent misfiled two thirds of the bucket.

DC/AC fans, blowers, heat sinks, thermal interface materials, Peltier modules, temperature sensors. dubIS's Mechanical & Hardware is fastening/mounting hardware (spacer, standoff, nut, washer, battery holder), so it is not an honest home for a fan; LCSC scores heat sinks {Mechanical & Hardware, Other} - even the hand-tuned table will not commit - and consumables {Other, Mechanical}. No single parent.

Fiber optic cables, connectors, transceiver/transmitter-receiver modules and amplifiers. The existing tables put these in two different parents: DigiKey 'Fiber Optic Connectors' -> {Connectors}, LCSC 'Fiber Optical Transceivers' -> {ICs - Interface, Other}. One Mouser umbrella spans both, so the parent row would contradict whichever half it picked.

Mouser's Frequency Control is crystals, resonators and oscillators (crystal/TCXO/VCXO/OCXO/MEMS), which is exactly dubIS's Crystals & Oscillators; the LCSC equivalents ('Crystals, Oscillators, Resonators', 'Resonators/Oscillators') are scored {Crystals & Oscillators} alone. Caveat for whoever adds subcategory rows: a leaf holding clock/timing ICs (PLL, clock generators, buffers) belongs to ICs - Interface, the split the DigiKey table already makes for 'Clock/Timing / Clock Generators, PLLs, Frequency Synthesizers'.

Mouser's interconnect tree is connectors, headers, terminals, cable assemblies - dubIS Connectors is the home for the bulk, and dubIS already reads 'connector/header/receptacle/terminal block' into it. The wire & cable and board-spacer/standoff children read as Other or Mechanical & Hardware and want their own rows.

Finished luminaires (bulbs, tubes, panels, fixtures) mixed with LED engines and lighting drivers. dubIS LEDs is for LED components and a lighting driver is a power IC (categorize.py routes 'lighting driver' there), so no single parent is honest.

SECTION_ORDER has no memory section; mirrors the existing LCSC row "Memory": {OTH}, which the corpus already scores as correct. Holds across the whole bucket - EEPROM/flash/SRAM ICs, DRAM modules, cards and drives all land in Other.

Bulk is LED indication, LED displays/modules and laser parts, which dubIS files under LEDs (displays included - cf. LCSC 'LED Segment Displays': {LED, OTH}); same call as LCSC "Optoelectronics": {LED}. The optoisolator children belong in ICs - Interface and light pipes in Mechanical/Other.
Literal catch-all - says nothing about what a part is. Same treatment as LCSC 'Other'/'Others'/'' (None in the labels module).

Spans three separate dubIS sections (Passives - Resistors / Capacitors / Inductors) plus crystals, filters and trimmers. Any single parent misfiles the other two-thirds; needs Mouser's leaf category, not the top level.

Bare PCBs, prototyping/perfboard and stencils. dubIS has no PCB section and Mechanical & Hardware is reserved for hardware/fasteners (spacer, standoff, nut, washer); DigiKey's nearest row, 'Solder Stencils, Templates', is itself {OTH, MECH}. Cannot place from its words alone.

Batteries, cords, power entry, transformers and finished AC/DC and DC/DC supplies. Every dubIS power section is IC-only, so ICs - Power / Voltage Regulators would misfile each brick; LCSC's nearest rows are ambiguous too (Battery Products {MECH, CON, OTH}).

Antennas, coax, RF amplifiers, transceivers, SAW filters and RFID modules. dubIS has no RF section and LCSC's equivalent is scored as a genuine 3-way ambiguity (RF And Wireless {OTH, IF, AMP}); picking one parent would be a guess.

Top level over all ICs, discretes, discrete modules, RF semiconductors and FPGAs - spans 8+ dubIS sections (Diodes, Discrete Semiconductors, every ICs - *). Only the leaf path is mappable; abstain at this level.

Everything in the bucket is a sensor and dubIS's only sensor section already takes the non-IC ones: categorize.py files thermistor, hall effect, humidity, moisture and photointerrupter under ICs - Sensors. Same decision as LCSC "Sensors": {SEN}.

Instruments, probes, clips, test leads and calibration services. dubIS has no instrument section, and Development Boards, Kits, Programmers is for dev kits and programmers, not bench gear - routing there would be a guess.

Mouser root crumb, not a component type: hand tools, soldering/desoldering stations, calibration and repair services, ESD control, labels, storage, cleaning chemicals, fasteners, batteries, tool kits. dubIS's Mechanical & Hardware is a thin fastener section and honestly holds only a minority of this bucket; tools, services and chemicals have no dubIS home. Nearest LCSC analogue 'Consumables' is labelled {OTH, MECH} - the existing table itself refuses to pick one, so under a single-section schema this is an abstain, not 'Other'.

Mouser root crumb and an application grouping, not a part type: RF transceivers and modules, LoRa/BT/WiFi/cellular modules, antennas, LNAs, RF switches, SAW/ceramic filters, RF connectors and cable assemblies, wireless dev kits, RFID/NFC. It spans ICs - Amplifiers, ICs - Interface, Connectors, Development Boards, Kits, Programmers and Other at once. The existing table encodes exactly this ambiguity as a three-way set (LCSC 'RF And Wireless' -> {OTH, IF, AMP}); forcing one parent would silently misfile most of the bucket.

Mouser root crumb: whole 3D printers and kits, filament and resin, print heads/nozzles, build surfaces, pens, post-processing consumables. dubIS is a parts inventory - a printer is a machine and filament is a consumable, so neither Mechanical & Hardware (fasteners/hardware) nor Development Boards, Kits, Programmers (dev tools and boards) is an honest home for the bucket as a whole.

Mouser's root catalogue bucket - semiconductors, passives, connectors, electromechanical, optoelectronics, displays and boards all sit under it. Mapping it to any single section would misfile nearly every part beneath it. This is the textbook catch-all the labels module gives None: 'Other': None, 'Others': None, 'Global Sourcing Parts': None.
